# bayesEfron

A meta-analysis or a multisite trial gives an estimate and a standard
error for each site. The usual random-effects model assumes that the
true effects behind the estimates follow a normal distribution.
bayesEfron fits the same model without that assumption. It estimates the
distribution of true effects, which may be skewed or have more than one
peak, together with the effect of each site. The distribution is
represented by Efron’s log-spline family and the model is fully
Bayesian, so that the intervals for the site effects include the
uncertainty about the distribution ([Lee and Sui,
2025](https://doi.org/10.3390/math13162639)).

## Installation

You can install bayesEfron from GitHub with:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("joonho112/bayesEfron")
```

The vignettes are on the [package
website](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/). To install them with
the package, you need knitr, rmarkdown and Pandoc (RStudio includes
Pandoc). Then add `build_vignettes = TRUE` to the call above.

Fitting a model also requires the cmdstanr package and CmdStan, neither
of which is on CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("cmdstanr",
                 repos = c("https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()
```

CmdStan is built from source and needs a C++ toolchain. Use
[`cmdstanr::check_cmdstan_toolchain()`](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/reference/install_cmdstan.html)
to check whether you have one. The cmdstanr [Getting started
article](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/articles/cmdstanr.html) describes
the installation and points to the requirements for each operating
system. The bayesEfron examples and vignettes run without CmdStan.

## Example

The data set `krw_discrimination` contains estimates for 97 large U.S.
firms from the correspondence experiment of [Kline, Rose and Walters
(2022)](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjac024). For each firm, `yi` is the
difference between the callback rates of job applications with
distinctively white and distinctively Black names, and `sei` is its
standard error, clustered by job vacancy. A positive gap favors
applications with white names, and 0.02 is a gap of 2 percentage points.
The sample follows the authors’ [2024
analysis](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20230700), and the estimates come
from the public replication code that accompanies [Walters
(2024)](https://doi.org/10.1016/bs.heslab.2024.11.001). [Lee and Sui
(2025)](https://doi.org/10.3390/math13162639) analyze these data with
this model.

``` r

library(bayesEfron)
head(krw_discrimination[, c("firm_name", "yi", "sei")], 3)
#>           firm_name         yi        sei
#> 1          Rite Aid 0.04695712 0.01619358
#> 2               KFC 0.02200000 0.01530472
#> 3 Victoria's Secret 0.04216161 0.02296031
```

We fit the model with
[`bayes_efron_fit()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/bayes_efron_fit.md).
This call requires CmdStan, and the first call compiles the Stan
program, which can take up to a minute.

``` r

dat <- as_bef_data(krw_discrimination, site = "firm_name")
fit <- bayes_efron_fit(dat, seed = 20250807)
```

The result of this call is included in the package as `krw_fit` (thinned
to 800 draws), so the rest of the example runs without CmdStan.

``` r

fit <- krw_fit
fit
#> <bayesEfron fit>
#> Model family: RE
#> Sites: 97
#> Grid method: pilot
#> Runtime: 0.7197 sec
#> Draws: 800 (4 chains, one iteration in 15 kept); site-level draws not kept
#> Diagnostics: Rhat 1.002; ESS bulk 1731; ESS tail 1780; divergences 0; treedepth hits 0
#> Standard errors: 0.005344 to 0.0392 (largest / smallest 7.335)
#> Grid: 101 points from -0.0829 to 0.1585; smallest standard error 2.213 grid spacings
#> Grid range: rule "pilot", not narrowed (the range of "paper_realdata"); point masses; 6 spline functions
#> Next: summary() and site_summary() for the sites, g_summary() for the distribution of effects, plot().
```

[`g_summary()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/g_summary.md)
summarizes the distribution of the gaps across firms. Here we ask for
its mean, variance and standard deviation on the percentage-point scale,
and for the proportion of firms with a positive gap. Each row has a
posterior mean and a 90% posterior interval.

``` r

g_summary(fit, type = "moments", scale = 100)
#>   parameter     mean    lower    upper
#> 1    mean_g 1.660178 1.308119 2.064913
#> 2     var_g 3.076948 1.399332 5.738865
#> 3      sd_g 1.716216 1.182933 2.395593
g_summary(fit, type = "prob", lower = 0)
#>   from  to      mean     lower     upper
#> 1    0 Inf 0.8754888 0.8083673 0.9366439
```

[`site_summary()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/site_summary.md)
returns posterior summaries of the gap at each firm, and
[`exceedance_prob()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/site_summary.md)
the posterior probability that a gap is positive.

``` r

sites <- site_summary(fit, scale = 100)
head(sites[, c("label", "estimate", "se", "mean", "lower", "upper")], 4)
#>               label  estimate       se     mean      lower    upper
#> 1          Rite Aid 4.6957123 1.619358 3.048175  1.0775168 5.349968
#> 2               KFC 2.2000000 1.530472 1.786494  0.1227187 3.581179
#> 3 Victoria's Secret 4.2161613 2.296031 2.334782  0.2864899 4.801767
#> 4    United Rentals 0.5708306 1.504751 1.071991 -0.5107269 2.719213
exceedance_prob(fit, sites = c("Rite Aid", "KFC"))
#>  Rite Aid       KFC 
#> 0.9967216 0.9624721
```

Finally, we plot the estimated distribution together with the normal
distribution of a random-effects model.

``` r

plot_g(fit, normal = TRUE, scale = 100) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "White-minus-Black callback gap (percentage points)")
```

![The estimated density of the callback gaps of 97 firms in percentage
points, with its 90% band, and the dashed curve of a normal distribution
fitted to the same
estimates.](reference/figures/README-callback-gaps-1.png)

The solid curve is the posterior mean of the density of the gaps, and
the band is a pointwise 90% posterior interval. The dashed curve is the
normal distribution of the usual random-effects model, with its mean and
standard deviation estimated by restricted maximum likelihood and shown
without their uncertainty. The model is free to depart from the normal
shape, and the band shows how well the data determine that shape: better
in the center, where the band is narrow relative to the height of the
curve, than in the tails.

## A distribution with two groups

`twin_towers` is a simulated data set of 1,500 sites from the public
replication files of Lee and Sui (2025), in which the true effects form
two groups. In
[`vignette("twin-towers")`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/twin-towers.md)
we fit it with the grid chosen from the estimates alone, as we would for
real data, and compare the result with the true effects.

![The estimated density of the effects of 1,500 simulated sites with its
band, a histogram of the true effects in two groups, and the dashed
curve of a normal distribution.](reference/figures/twin-towers.png)

The largest standard error is nine times the smallest, and for about one
site in seven it is larger than the gap between the two groups. The
fitted density has a peak over each group and little mass between them,
which a normal distribution, with its single peak, cannot have. This is
a single data set; see
[`vignette("implementation")`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/implementation.md)
for how often the 90% intervals contain the true effects across
simulated data sets, including the settings in which their coverage
falls short of 90%.

## Learning more

- [Getting started with
  bayesEfron](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/bayesEfron.html)
  walks through the analysis of the 97 firms, from preparing the data to
  summarizing the results.
- [Choosing the grid and checking sensitivity to
  it](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/choosing-a-grid.html)
  discusses how the results can depend on the grid.
- [Checking a
  fit](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/diagnostics.html)
  covers the diagnostics.

The [package website](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/) lists the
other vignettes. It also has a case study that is not installed with the
package: the effect of small classes in the 79 schools of Tennessee’s
Project STAR, a multisite trial in education. The estimates for that
case study are in `star_schools`.

## Citation

To cite the package, cite the paper, as `citation("bayesEfron")` shows:

> Lee, J. and Sui, D. (2025). Fully Bayesian inference for meta-analytic
> deconvolution using Efron’s log-spline prior. *Mathematics*, 13(16),
> 2639. <https://doi.org/10.3390/math13162639>

Department of Education, through Grant R305D240078 to the University of

# Package index

## Fit the model

[`bayes_efron_fit()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/bayes_efron_fit.md)
fits the model.
[`?bef_fit`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/bef_fit.md)
describes the fitted object and its methods.

  : Fit the Bayesian Efron log-spline model to estimates and standard
  errors

## Prepare the data and the grid

Check the estimates and their standard errors, and build the grid and
the spline basis on which the distribution of effects is represented.

- [`as_bef_data()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/as_bef_data.md)
  [`print(`*`<bef_data>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/as_bef_data.md)
  [`summary(`*`<bef_data>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/as_bef_data.md)
  [`format(`*`<bef_data>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/as_bef_data.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<bef_data>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/as_bef_data.md)
  : Extract estimates and standard errors from a data frame or list
- [`make_efron_grid()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/make_efron_grid.md)
  [`format(`*`<bef_grid>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/make_efron_grid.md)
  [`print(`*`<bef_grid>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/make_efron_grid.md)
  : Build the grid and spline basis for the distribution of effects

## Summarize a fit

The estimated distribution of effects and the posterior distributions of
the site effects, as data frames.

- [`g_summary()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/g_summary.md)
  : Summarize the estimated distribution of effects
- [`site_summary()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/site_summary.md)
  [`exceedance_prob()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/site_summary.md)
  : Summarize the posterior distributions of the site effects

  [`as.data.frame(`*`<bef_diagnostic>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/diagnose.md)
  [`format(`*`<bef_diagnostic>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/diagnose.md)
  [`nuts_params(`*`<bef_fit>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/diagnose.md)
  [`log_posterior(`*`<bef_fit>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/diagnose.md)
  [`rhat(`*`<bef_fit>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/diagnose.md)
  [`neff_ratio(`*`<bef_fit>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/diagnose.md)
  : MCMC convergence and grid diagnostics for a fitted model

## Plots

Each plot function returns a `ggplot` object.
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) on a fit calls
them by `type`.

- [`plot(`*`<bef_fit_re>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot.bef_fit_re.md)
  : Plot a fitted model

### Results

- [`plot_g()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_g.md)
  : Density and CDF plots of the estimated distribution of effects
- [`plot_sites()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_sites.md)
  : Caterpillar (forest) plot of the site effects
- [`plot_shrinkage()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_shrinkage.md)
  : Shrinkage plot of posterior means against estimates
- [`plot_exceedance()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_exceedance.md)
  : Plot the exceedance probabilities of the site effects
- [`plot_site_posterior()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_site_posterior.md)
  : Plot the posterior distribution of individual site effects

### Checks of a fit

- [`plot_diagnostics()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_diagnostics.md)
  : Plot sampler diagnostics and grid diagnostics
- [`plot_loo()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_loo.md)
  : Plot the Pareto k values of leave-one-out cross-validation
- [`plot_ppc()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_ppc.md)
  : Posterior predictive check
- [`plot_mcmc()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_mcmc.md)
  : Trace plots and other MCMC plots with bayesplot

### Grids and simulated data

- [`plot(`*`<bef_grid>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot.bef_grid.md)
  : Plot a grid and its spline basis with the estimates
- [`plot(`*`<bef_grid_comparison>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot.bef_grid_comparison.md)
  : Plot the sensitivity of the results to the grid
- [`plot_recovery()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/plot_recovery.md)
  : Plot the recovery of true effects in simulated data

## Compare models

Leave-one-out cross-validation, a comparison of fits with different
grids and spline bases, and the estimate of g in the form that the
empirical Bayes functions of the ebnm package take.

- [`loo(`*`<bef_fit>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/loo.bef_fit.md)
  [`waic(`*`<bef_fit>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/loo.bef_fit.md)
  : Leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC for a fitted model
- [`compare_efron_grids()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/compare_efron_grids.md)
  [`print(`*`<bef_grid_comparison>`*`)`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/compare_efron_grids.md)
  : Compare fits on several grids (sensitivity analysis)
- [`as_normalmix()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/as_normalmix.md)
  : Export the estimated distribution of effects for the ebnm package

## Compile the model

Compile the Stan program before the first fit, or delete the compiled
model.

- [`bayes_efron_compile()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/bayes_efron_compile.md)
  [`bayes_efron_clear_cache()`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/bayes_efron_compile.md)
  : Compile the Stan programs before the first fit

## Data sets and stored fits

Example data, and fits of them that are stored in the package so that
the examples run without CmdStan.

### Callback gaps of 97 firms, and 1,500 simulated sites (Lee and Sui, 2025)

- [`krw_discrimination`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/krw_discrimination.md)
  : Racial callback gaps among 97 large firms
- [`krw_fit`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/krw_fit.md)
  : Model fitted to the racial callback gaps
- [`twin_towers`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/twin_towers.md)
  : Twin Towers simulated data
- [`twin_towers_fit`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/twin_towers_fit.md)
  : Model fitted to the Twin Towers simulated data

### A small meta-analysis (19 teacher expectancy studies)

- [`raudenbush1985`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/raudenbush1985.md)
  : Teacher expectancy studies
- [`raudenbush_fit`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/raudenbush_fit.md)
  : Model fitted to the teacher expectancy studies

### A multisite trial in education (79 schools of Project STAR)

- [`star_schools`](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/reference/star_schools.md)
  : Small-class effects in 79 schools of Project STAR

# Articles

### Case studies

- [Twin Towers: recovering a distribution hidden by
  noise](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/twin-towers.md):

  A simulated data set of 1,500 sites with known true effects in two
  separated groups, fitted from the estimates and standard errors alone.

- [Nineteen studies of teacher
  expectancy](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/teacher-expectancy.md):

  A case study of a meta-analysis with 19 studies: the estimated
  distribution of effects, its sensitivity to the range of the grid, and
  a simulation study of fits of this size.

- [Small classes in 79
  schools](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/class-size.md):

  Analyze a multisite trial in education: build an estimate and a
  standard error for each of 79 schools from student data, fit the
  model, and use alternative standard errors and a simulation with known
  effects to judge the evidence that the effect of small classes varies
  across schools.

- [bayesEfron and empirical Bayes methods
  compared](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/empirical-bayes.md):

  bayesEfron and the empirical Bayes methods in the ebnm package, fitted
  to the same data: agreement of the posterior means, differences in the
  intervals and in the estimated distribution of effects, and the
  contribution of the uncertainty about that distribution.

### Guides

- [Estimates, standard errors and site
  labels](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/data-input.md):

  Getting estimates and standard errors into a fit from a data frame,
  two vectors or metafor, and keeping the names of the sites through to
  the tables and plots.

- [Plots of a fitted
  model](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/plots.md):

  A gallery of the plot functions: the question that each answers, the
  call, and what the result shows.

- [Choosing the grid and checking sensitivity to
  it](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/choosing-a-grid.md):

  The choices that define the grid, the default method for its range,
  checks of the range after a fit, and a comparison of results across
  grids.

- [Checking a
  fit](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/diagnostics.md):

  Sampler diagnostics, grid diagnostics, a posterior predictive check,
  and how to respond to a warning.

- [The model and the posterior distribution of a site
  effect](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/model.md):

  The deconvolution problem, the log-spline family for the distribution
  of effects, its prior, and the posterior distribution of a site
  effect.

- [Reproducibility and interval
  coverage](https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/articles/implementation.md):

  Reproducing a fit, the draws stored in a fit, the two Stan programs,
  checks of the computations, interval coverage in simulated data, and
  the relation to the paper.
